q: The Vitali covering theorem states: given a collection 𝒱 of balls covering a set E ⊂ ℝⁿ in the Vitali sense, there exists a countable disjoint subcollection {Bₖ} ⊂ 𝒱 such that:
exp: Vitali's covering theorem: from a Vitali cover (every point is in arbitrarily small balls of 𝒱) one extracts a disjoint subcollection whose 5-fold dilates cover the whole set. This is the foundation of Lebesgue differentiation theorem.
